### ⭐⭐ The row I nearly got wrong, and the thing this PR did that stops the next reader getting it wrong too

My first pass measured bare `${user.` at **5 → 4** and I went looking for four unfixed sites. They are not unfixed. Read at source:

```
packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx:826-827   `current_user` is aliased to `user` so both `user.email` and `current_user.email` …
packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx:843       current_user: (predicateScope as any)?.user,
```

⇒ **`user` IS a legitimate scope root** — the *signed-in user*, published by the host's `ExpressionProvider`. The four survivors are all ambient-user reads (`user.role`, `user.firstName`/`lastName`, `user.isAdmin`) and are **right**. The card's defect was `${user.name}` standing in for **record data**, which merely shared the prefix.

⭐ And this is exactly what your unasked-for addition buys:

> `:106` The scope the evaluator builds holds four names, and nothing else:
> `:113` | `current_user` (aliased to `user`) | the signed-in user, published by the host's `ExpressionProvider` — **not by anything on this page** |

That is the same both-coordinates rule the fence set, applied to the sweep.

Saying so makes the repaired page's claim precise — clean on the wiring coordinate everywhere, clean on both coordinates in its three named passages.
